const matchesLowStock = !showLowStock || p.stock < 5; // Low stock threshold 5 return matchesSearch && matchesCategory && matchesLowStock; }); }); onSearchChange(val: string) { this.searchTerm.set(val); } handleBarcodeScan() { const barcode = this.searchTerm(); if (!barcode) return; const success = this.posService.addToCartByBarcode(barcode); // Force clear the input using nativeElement for speed (critical for scanners) if (this.barcodeInput) { this.barcodeInput.nativeElement.value = ''; this.barcodeInput.nativeElement.focus(); } // Also update the signal this.searchTerm.set(''); if (success) { this.playBeep(); } } setCurrency(curr: 'MMK' | 'THB' | 'CNY') { this.posService.activeCurrency.set(curr); } selectPayment(method: 'Cash' | 'KBZ Pay' | 'Wave Pay' | 'Credit') { this.selectedPayment.set(method); } processPayment() { this.speakTotal(); const order = this.posService.checkout(this.selectedPayment()); if (order) { this.lastOrder.set(order); this.showPaymentModal.set(false); this.selectedPayment.set('Cash'); // Clear discount after sale this.posService.setDiscount(0); this.posService.selectedCustomerId.set(null); // Reset customer } } // --- New Features --- toggleDiscount() { this.tempDiscount = this.posService.cartDiscount(); this.showDiscountModal.set(true); } setQuickDiscount(percentage: number) { const subtotal = this.posService.cartSubTotalMMK(); this.tempDiscount = Math.floor(subtotal * percentage); } applyDiscount() { if(this.tempDiscount < 0) this.tempDiscount = 0; this.posService.setDiscount(this.tempDiscount); this.showDiscountModal.set(false); } selectCustomer(cust: Customer | null) { this.posService.selectCustomerForCart(cust ? cust.id : null); this.showCustomerModal.set(false); } getCustomerName(id: number): string { return this.posService.customers().find(c => c.id === id)?.name || 'Unknown'; } parkCurrentOrder() { if(confirm('လက်ရှိဘေလ်ကို ခေတ္တသိမ်းထားမည်လား?')) { this.posService.parkOrder(`Bill #${Math.floor(Math.random()*1000)}`); } } retrieveParked(id: number) { if(this.posService.cart().length > 0) { if(!confirm('လက်ရှိခြင်းတောင်းကို ဖျက်ပြီး သိမ်းထားသောဘေလ်ကို ပြန်ယူမည်လား?')) return; } this.posService.retrieveOrder(id); this.showParkedModal.set(false); } // Rate Edit Logic openRateModal() { // Just open modal, user can see/edit all this.showRateModal.set(true); } updateRate(currency: 'THB' | 'CNY', val: number) { if (val > 0) { this.posService.updateExchangeRate(currency, val); } } saveRate() { this.showRateModal.set(false); } // Helper to calculate cross rates dynamically based on MMK base calculateCrossRate(from: 'THB' | 'CNY', to: 'THB' | 'CNY'): number { const rates = this.posService.exchangeRates(); // e.g. 1 CNY (450 MMK) -> ? THB (100 MMK) // 450 / 100 = 4.5 return rates[from] / rates[to]; } // New helper in component calculateMMKToForeign(amount: number, currency: 'THB' | 'CNY'): number { const rate = this.posService.exchangeRates()[currency]; if(!rate) return 0; return amount / rate; } // Helper for footer display getConvertedTotal(targetCurrency: 'THB' | 'CNY'): number { const mmkTotal = this.posService.cartTotalMMK(); const rate = this.posService.exchangeRates()[targetCurrency]; return Math.ceil(mmkTotal / rate); } playBeep() { const ctx = new (window.AudioContext || (window as any).webkitAudioContext)(); const osc = ctx.createOscillator(); osc.connect(ctx.destination); osc.frequency.value = 800; osc.start(); osc.stop(0.1); } speakTotal() { if ('speechSynthesis' in window) { const total = this.posService.convertPrice(this.posService.cartTotalMMK()); const currency = this.posService.activeCurrency(); let text = ''; if (currency === 'MMK') text = `Total is ${total} Kyats`; else if (currency === 'THB') text = `Total is ${total} Baht`; else text = `Total is ${total} Yuan`; const utterance = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance(text); window.speechSynthesis.speak(utterance); } } // --- Product Management Logic --- onFileSelected(event: any) { const file = event.target.files[0]; if (file) { if (file.size > 500000) { // Limit 500KB to save localStorage alert('ဓာတ်ပုံဖိုင်ဆိုဒ် ကြီးလွန်းပါသည်။ 500KB အောက်ပုံကို ရွေးပါ။'); return; } const reader = new FileReader(); reader.onload = (e: any) => { this.modalProductImage = e.target.result; }; reader.readAsDataURL(file); } } openProductModal(productData?: Product) { if (productData) { // IMPORTANT: Fetch the latest data from the service to ensure we have current Stock // The productData passed from the template loop might be stale if checkout happened recently const freshProduct = this.posService.products().find(p => p.id === productData.id) || productData; this.isEditing.set(true); this.editingProductId = freshProduct.id; this.modalProductBarcode = freshProduct.barcode; this.modalProductName = freshProduct.name; this.modalProductPrice = freshProduct.price; this.modalProductCost = freshProduct.cost || 0; this.modalProductStock = freshProduct.stock; this.modalProductCategory = freshProduct.category; this.modalProductImage = freshProduct.image; } else { // Check limit if adding new if (!this.posService.isProVersion() && this.posService.products().length >= 5) { alert("Free Version တွင် ပစ္စည်း ၅ မျိုးသာ ထည့်သွင်းခွင့်ရှိသည်။"); return; } this.isEditing.set(false); this.editingProductId = null; this.modalProductBarcode = ''; this.modalProductName = ''; this.modalProductPrice = 0; this.modalProductCost = 0; this.modalProductStock = 0; this.modalProductCategory = 'Other'; this.modalProductImage = ''; } this.showProductModal.set(true); } closeProductModal() { this.showProductModal.set(false); } submitProduct() { if (!this.modalProductName || this.modalProductPrice <= 0) { alert('Please fill all required fields correctly.'); return; } const imageToSave = this.modalProductImage || `https://picsum.photos/200/200?random=${Date.now()}`; if (this.isEditing() && this.editingProductId) { const updated: Product = { id: this.editingProductId, name: this.modalProductName, price: this.modalProductPrice, cost: this.modalProductCost, stock: this.modalProductStock, category: this.modalProductCategory, barcode: this.modalProductBarcode, image: imageToSave }; this.posService.updateProduct(updated); } else { this.posService.addNewProduct( this.modalProductName, this.modalProductPrice, this.modalProductCost, this.modalProductCategory, this.modalProductBarcode, this.modalProductStock, imageToSave ); } this.closeProductModal(); } deleteProduct() { if (this.editingProductId && confirm('Are you sure you want to delete this product?')) { this.posService.deleteProduct(this.editingProductId); this.closeProductModal(); } } printReceipt() { window.print(); } }

payload.text: ငွေကြေးတွေသတ်မှတ်တွက်ချက်တာတွေမှာလွဲနေတယ် ပစ္စည်းတန်ဖိုးက ကျပ်/ဘတ်/ယွမ် ကိုကြိုက်တာထားလို့ရရမှာလေ အခုဟာက ပစ္စည်းမှာ ကျပ်နဲ့ဘဲသတ်မှတ်လို့ရတယ် ကျွန်တော်တို့က နယ်စပ်မှာသုံးမှာဖြစ်တဲ့အတွက် အကုန်စိတ်ကြိုက်သတ်မှတ်လို့ရရမှာ

**Considering the Core Issue**

I'm currently focused on the user's core problem, which is the system's reliance on a single MMK base price for all conversions. I'm starting to deconstruct how this impacts pricing accuracy and considering if there are better solutions, perhaps incorporating more granular exchange rate data. The goal is to identify points of improvement to propose to the user.


**Evaluating Currency Flexibility**

I'm now thinking about how the border context affects pricing. It seems the user wants direct price setting in various currencies, MMK, THB, or CNY, not just conversions from a MMK base. I'm leaning toward a `Product` interface update. We could either support a selected currency for each price or store prices in all currencies. The border scenario points toward a base currency per item, with conversions happening only at the point of sale. I need to make sure the Product's interface has the flexibility for each situation.


**Implementing Currency Solutions**

I'm now outlining the steps to integrate multi-currency support. I plan to add a `currency` field to the `Product` model and update both the `PosService` and UI components to handle currency selection during product creation and editing. Next, the calculations need to be updated to ensure values are normalized appropriately, especially for totals. The UI updates will include currency selection in product creation, and displaying prices in their original currency within the product grid, while the cart will convert to the active currency, ideally including the original. I'm leaning towards the preferred Option B (1 Price + 1 Currency) to avoid data entry issues.


**Detailing the Conversion Logic**

I've been working through the implementation details for multi-currency handling. I've considered that the ideal approach involves adding a `priceCurrency` field to the `Product` interface. I'm moving toward creating a `convertPriceToActive` method within `PosService` to handle currency conversions, likely normalizing everything to MMK internally for calculations and totals before displaying in the active currency. I'm focusing now on the best implementation of the helper function for MMK conversion.


**Developing Conversion Functions**

I'm now building out the conversion logic. The plan is to add a `currency` field to the `Product` interface and then update the `PosService`. The `calculateMMKValue` function will handle the conversions: if the product's price is in MMK, it'll return the price as-is. If THB or CNY, the function will convert it to MMK using the stored exchange rates. Then, `convertPrice` will translate to the active display currency. I'm focusing on ensuring these steps will produce accurate results.


**Implementing UI Currency Updates**

I'm now detailing updates for the UI to support multi-currency. I plan to modify the `pos-terminal.component.ts` file. Specifically, I'll add a currency selection dropdown to the product modal. The product grid will display prices with the appropriate currency symbols, such as 100 ฿. The cart view will include the original price along with its currency. The totals will be handled by the service, and the component will only display the resulting values after conversion.


**Finalizing Code Modifications**

I'm solidifying the planned code updates, beginning with the service files. The `Product` interface will gain a `currency` field that can accept 'MMK', 'THB', or 'CNY' values. I'll modify the `calculateMMKValue` function and update the cart totals to use this function. In the UI component, I will add currency selection to the product modal, load currency during modal opening, pass the currency on submit, and display the price with the corresponding symbol in the product grid.


**Finalizing Implementation Steps**

I'm now detailing the final implementation steps. I've considered that the `PosService` needs an update, including the `Product` interface. I'll add a helper function `getMMKValue(amount, currency)`, and I'll update `cartSubTotalMMK` and `cartTotalCostMMK` to use this helper. The product card and cart item will be updated to show the original currency in the component. I'm checking the results against project rules and formatting.


**Refining Input Clarity**

I'm now focusing on how the UI clarifies currency selection, particularly in the product input. I realize the user wants to directly define prices in any currency. I'll need to update input labels in line with the currency dropdown to ensure the UX is clear. The plan to add a `currency` property to the `Product` interface will facilitate the implementation of the currency requirements.


**Initiating Code Implementation**

I'm starting the code implementation now. I'm focusing on the `PosService` and UI components. The `Product` interface will now include a `currency` field. The `calculateMMKValue` method will return the amount converted to MMK using the correct exchange rate. I am working on how to properly calculate the `cartSubTotalMMK` and `cartTotalCostMMK` signals, as well as updating the `addNewProduct` and `updateProduct` functions to handle the new field. I'm prioritizing the UI updates too, including adding the currency select box to the product modal.

မိတ်ဆွေ ပြောတာအလွန်မှန်ပါတယ်။ နယ်စပ်ဒေသတွေမှာ ပစ္စည်းတစ်ခုချင်းစီရဲ့ မူရင်းဈေးနှုန်းကို **ကျပ်၊ ဘတ်၊ ယွမ်** ကြိုက်ရာနဲ့ သတ်မှတ်ထားလေ့ရှိပါတယ်။ ဥပမာ - ထိုင်းပစ္စည်းဆို ဘတ်နဲ့ဈေးသတ်မှတ်မယ်၊ တရုတ်ပစ္စည်းဆို ယွမ်နဲ့သတ်မှတ်မယ်၊ မြန်မာပစ္စည်းဆို ကျပ်နဲ့သတ်မှတ်မယ်။ ရောင်းတဲ့အချိန်ကျမှ ငွေလဲနှုန်းအလိုက် တွက်ချက်ရမှာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။

ဒါကြောင့် အောက်ပါပြောင်းလဲမှုတွေကို ပြုလုပ်ပေးလိုက်ပါတယ် -

1.  **Product Setup:** ပစ္စည်းအသစ်ထည့်တဲ့အခါ **ဈေးနှုန်း (Price)** နဲ့ **အရင်း (Cost)** ကို ဘယ်ငွေကြေး (Currency) နဲ့ သတ်မှတ်မလဲဆိုတာ ရွေးလို့ရအောင် ပြင်ပေးထားပါတယ်။
2.  **Calculation Logic:** စက်က တွက်ချက်တဲ့အခါ ပစ္စည်းရဲ့ မူရင်းငွေကြေး (ဥပမာ - ၁၀ ဘတ်) ကို ယူပြီး၊ လက်ရှိသတ်မှတ်ထားတဲ့ ငွေလဲနှုန်း (Exchange Rate) နဲ့မြှောက်ပြီးမှ စုစုပေါင်းသင့်ငွေ (Total) ကို တွက်ထုတ်ပေးမှာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။
3.  **Display:** ပစ္စည်းကဒ်ပြားလေးတွေပေါ်မှာ မူရင်းသတ်မှတ်ထားတဲ့ ဈေးနှုန်း (ဥပမာ - 100 ฿ သို့မဟုတ် 5 ¥) အတိုင်း ပြသပေးထားပါမယ်။

**Assessing User Input**

I'm currently focused on the user's difficulties with entering the shop name in Burmese. My initial assessment is that font support within the application might be the core issue. I'm considering the possibility of encoding discrepancies or a lack of appropriate Burmese fonts. This could be causing display problems.


**Analyzing Interface Changes**

I'm now investigating how to implement the QR code image upload feature. The user's preference for static QR codes is a solid direction. My focus is on modifying the `ShopConfig` interface to accommodate image storage. I also need to update the `shopInfo` signal initialization, along with ensuring the font `Padauk` is applied consistently.


**Developing Implementation Strategy**

I'm now deep-diving into the implementation plan. I'm focusing on the service modifications to include fields for the KBZ Pay and Wave Pay QR images. I'll update `updateShopInfo` to handle the new QR image data. Then I will add file inputs in the dashboard for image uploads and store these images as base64 strings in the service. My current design will update the payment modal to display the appropriate uploaded QR codes, or a fallback if there's no uploaded image. I'm going to double-check that the Burmese shop name input works correctly too.


**Refining QR Code Display**

I'm now in the process of refining the QR code display logic. I'm focusing on ensuring that the KBZ Pay and Wave Pay QR images are rendered correctly within the POS terminal's payment UI. I will update the `shopInfo` class. I also need to ensure the correct QR code is displayed based on the payment method selected. I'll double-check font inheritance for Burmese shop names.


**Evaluating Image Optimization**

I'm now assessing how to optimize the storage and handling of uploaded QR codes. My immediate concern is the size of the Base64 strings, especially with the potential for high-resolution images. I need to implement a check or warning to address the risk of exceeding the LocalStorage limit. I intend to add image size checks during upload, similar to the product image logic I previously implemented, capping the file size to 500KB. I'll make sure to apply the `Padauk` font on all the inputs on the dashboard.


**Crafting the Implementation**

I'm now in the process of finalizing the code changes. I'm focusing on creating `pos.service.ts` to update the interface. I'll add file handlers and the UI for uploading QR codes to the dashboard component. And, I'm going to update the payment modal in the `pos-terminal.component.ts` to display the stored images. I'm making sure to explicitly set the `Padauk` font for the shop name input to ensure Burmese text renders correctly.

payload.text: Admin Control Panelမှာလစည်ကြေးဖြစ်တဲ့အတွက် Keyမှာရက်စွဲနဲ့အလုပ်လုပ်ရမှာမလား

**Defining Subscription Mechanics**

I'm now focusing on the "Admin Control Panel" and its subscription model. I'm drilling down on the subscription/license key mechanism, specifically considering the implications of a "monthly fee."


**Evolving License Validation**

I'm now thinking the license key should be date-based, not just a static string, to reflect the monthly subscription. My code currently uses a simple equality check in `PosService`. The next step is to modify this to validate an expiry date. The previous model used the `enteredLicense` signal, but it has to be updated. It looks like I have a bit more work to do on the license validation, to get it working in the Admin Control Panel.


**Implementing Date Validation**

Okay, I've got a clearer picture now. The goal is to move from a string-based license to a date-driven expiry system within the `Admin Control Panel`. Instead of simply checking if the entered license matches a required one, I'm setting an expiration date when the admin updates their license. The system will then compare today's date against that expiration date to determine if the license is valid.


**Analyzing Date Logic**

I'm now refining the date logic for the license system. If today is less than the expiration date, then the application should use the pro features. I'm considering an encrypted key approach for date storage, but it might be too complex for the user. I've decided to move away from a "Target License Key" field and use a "Valid Until" date in the admin panel. The application will store this date, and `isProVersion` will check validity. The admin panel is assumed to be protected, perhaps accessed by the *Software Provider*. The *Provider* could enter a special key to set this date.


**Developing Key Mechanism**

I've been iterating on the "Key" approach and have simplified it. Now, the admin enters a "Magic Code" or license key, and I'm planning a system where the expiry date is derived from this key. The key format will be `EXP:YYYYMMDD`, encoded using Base64 for basic obfuscation. This will allow the system to decode and validate the expiry date, updating the `licenseExpiryDate` in local storage for the `PosService`.


**Refining Key Derivation**

I'm now simplifying the license key format further. I've moved away from checksums for ease of use. The revised format is `FW-YYYYMMDD`, making it straightforward for the admin to generate or for me to create a helper for generating. When a user enters it, I can parse it for validation. In the admin panel, I'm considering allowing them to directly set the expiration date, since they have the proper credentials.


**Revising Display Elements**

My current focus is on the user interface. I plan to update the display in the User/License section to show "Valid Until: [Date]" or "Expired". I'm removing the old "Key" matching, shifting to date-based expiry. The "key" now provides an extension mechanism. Specifically, a specially formatted key (e.g., `FW-EXTEND-30`) can extend validity. For simplicity, the Admin Panel will also get a date picker to set the expiry date.

I've also finalized the *Design*. My *Service* code will now replace the `requiredLicense` with a `licenseExpiryDate` variable. `isProVersion` will return true if today's date is before the expiration date. In the *Admin Panel*, the label "Set Valid License Key" changes to "Set Expiration Date" with a date picker.


**Expanding Activation Methods**

I'm now integrating remote activation support. The plan is to enable the shop owner to extend the license without needing admin access. I'm introducing a new key format: `PAY-YYYYMMDD`. When entered, the system will parse the date, set the `licenseExpiryDate` and extend the subscription if it's a valid key. The developer is the one using the admin panel to set up the machine. The workflow has been described: The developer sets an expiry date, and then the agent can extend the license remotely using the `PAY-YYYYMMDD` key.


**Updating UI and Logic**

I'm now revising my UI and code structure to align with the revised requirements. I'm focusing on the integration of the "PAY-YYYYMMDD" key for remote license extension, and a simple local method to specify the expiration date with the Admin Panel's date picker. I will also incorporate logic in the PosService to handle the extended license, which updates the expiry date.



**Implementing Code Changes**

I'm now implementing the code changes, as planned. The focus is now on *Service* and *Dashboard*. In `PosService`, I removed the license and added the new `licenseExpiryDate` and the date validation. I also created `attemptActivation` to parse the new key format. The admin panel now displays and edits the date, while the client license section shows expiry status. I'm updating `PosService` to handle the date format and implementing the changes in the admin panel to show/edit the new format.


**Adjusting Key Format**

I'm now revising the license key for simplicity and security. I've concluded that the `FW-YYYYMMDD` format is sufficiently user-friendly for now, avoiding unnecessary complexity like checksums or encryption. My main focus is on the client license section and the admin panel's date picker to manage expiration dates. I'm also updating the `dashboard.component.ts` to include this date-based input.

ဟုတ်ကဲ့ မိတ်ဆွေပြောတာ အလွန်မှန်ကန်ပါတယ်။ လစဉ်ကြေးပုံစံ (Subscription Model) သွားမယ်ဆိုရင် Key တစ်ခုတည်းနဲ့ မလုံလောက်တော့ပါဘူး။ ရက်စွဲ (Expiry Date) နဲ့ ထိန်းချုပ်တာက ပိုပြီး လက်တွေ့ကျပါတယ်။

ဒါကြောင့် အောက်ပါပြောင်းလဲမှုတွေကို ပြုလုပ်ပေးထားပါတယ် -

1.  **License System ပြောင်းလဲခြင်း:** အရင်လို Key တိုက်စစ်တဲ့ပုံစံမဟုတ်တော့ဘဲ **သက်တမ်းကုန်ဆုံးရက် (Expiry Date)** စနစ်ကို ပြောင်းလိုက်ပါမယ်။
2.  **Admin Panel:** ဆိုင်ပိုင်ရှင်/Admin ဘက်ကနေ ရက်စွဲကို တိုက်ရိုက် ပြင်လို့ရအောင် Date Picker ထည့်ပေးထားပါတယ်။
3.  **Activation Key:** ဖောက်သည် (ဆိုင်ရှင်) ကို Key ပေးတဲ့အခါ `FW` နောက်မှာ ရက်စွဲကပ်ပြီး ပေးလိုက်ရင် (ဥပမာ - `FW20241231`) စနစ်က အဲဒီရက်စွဲအထိ အလိုအလျောက် သက်တမ်းတိုးပေးသွားမှာ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။

အောက်ပါ Code များကို Update လုပ်ပေးပါ။
